problems.title: Move a signed factor inside a radical
problems.question: Move the factor in−0.5yx³√(−4y⁷/x⁵) inside the square root.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The domain is x≠0 and y/x≤0. Hence −0.5yx³≥0, so it may be squared inside the radical without an outside minus.

problems.title: Similarity and perimeter scale
problems.question: A triangle has side ratio3:4:6. A similar triangle has 3 times its perimeter and shortest side 12. Find the original longest side.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: All lengths scale by 3, so the original shortest side is 12/3=4.
steps: The longest/shortest ratio is 6/3=2. Hence the longest side is 8.

problems.title: A similarity with a shared angle
problems.question: D lies on BC,∠ADB=∠BAC, BD=4, DC=5. Find AB.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: Triangles ABD and CBA are similar:their B angles agree, and their D, A angles agree. Thus AB/BC=BD/AB.

problems.title: Product of equal-absolute-value roots
problems.question: Find the product of roots of|2x−1|=|x−2|.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
steps: The roots are −1 and 1, whose product is −1.

problems.title: A listed root of a radical inequality
problems.question: Which listed value solves(3−x)√x≥0?
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: Require x≥0. For x>0, the sign is that of 3−x, so the full set is[0,3].

problems.title: Natural-number roots between radicals
problems.question: Count positive-integer x satisfying√15<8−x≤√144.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: √144=12 gives x≥−4; the other inequality gives x<8−√15≈4.127.

problems.title: Trapezoid diagonal midpoints
problems.question: A trapezoid’s diagonals divide each other in ratio2:5. Their midpoints are 6 apart. Find the smaller base.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The base ratio is 2:5. Distance between diagonal midpoints is half the base difference.
steps: Write bases2t,5t. Then 3t/2=6, t=4, and the smaller base is 8.

problems.title: A line through half an altitude
problems.question: In an isosceles triangle, a line through the midpoint of the base altitude is parallel to one equal side. In what ratio does it divide the other side?
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The altitude meets the base midpoint. A parallel-section or coordinate calculation puts the intersection one quarter of the way down the other leg from the apex.
steps: For example use vertices(−1,0),(1,0),(0, h) and altitude midpoint(0, h/2). Solving the parallel-line intersection gives fraction1/4.
Thus the two parts have ratio1:3.

problems.title: An absolute value hidden in a square root

problems.title: Intersect two linear inequalities
problems.question: Count integer roots of(3−x)/2−(2−x)/3>−1 and x(x+1)<(x+1)².
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The first simplifies to x<11; the second to x>−1.
steps: The common interval is(−1,11), with integers 0 through10, eleven in all.

problems.title: A rectangle from coordinate inequalities
problems.question: Find the perimeter of the region|y|≤3,|x+1|≤5.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The rectangle has −3≤y≤3 and −6≤x≤4.
steps: Its width is 10, height 6, so perimeter2(10+6)=32.

problems.title: Trisect both diagonals
problems.question: Both diagonals of a parallelogram are trisected. Find the perimeter of the quadrilateral through the 4 trisection points if the original perimeter is 72.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The diagonal centre is common, and each trisection point is one third of the corresponding vertex’s distance from it.
steps: The inner quadrilateral is a homothetic copy with scale1/3. Its perimeter is 72/3=24.

problems.title: Incircle contact chord in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base12. The distance between the incircle contacts on its equal sides is 3. Find a leg.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: Let leg=s. Equal tangent lengths make each apex-to-contact segment s−6. The contact chord is parallel to the base.

problems.title: Negative integer radical-domain values
problems.question: For how many negative integers is √(|x−1|−4)/√(x+8) defined?
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The nonzero radical denominator requires x>−8. For negative x, the numerator requires1−x−4≥0, or x≤−3.

problems.title: A rational absolute-value equation
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of(x+5)/(|3−x|−2)=2.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: Exclude x=1,5. Multiplication gives x+9=2|3−x|.
steps: For x≤3, the equation gives x=−1. For x≥3, it gives x=15. Both avoid the exclusions.

problems.title: Match a solution half-line
problems.question: Find a such that3−4x>a−8 has solution x<−2.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: Rearranging gives x<(11−a)/4.
steps: Set the boundary equal to −2:11−a=−8, a=19.

problems.title: Similar triangles from two altitudes
problems.question: In acute ABC, AD and CE are altitudes. BD:ED=4:3 and AC=9. Find AB.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: A, D, E, C lie on the circle with diameter AC. This gives∠BDE=∠BAC, while the angle at B is shared.
steps: Thus triangles BDE and BAC are similar, and BD/DE=BA/AC. Hence AB=(4/3)·9=12.

problems.title: A parallel section of a trapezoid
problems.question: A line parallel to trapezoid bases divides the legs3:7 from the smaller base. Bases are 6,16. Find the section length.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The fraction of height from the small base is 3/(3+7)=3/10. Section lengths interpolate linearly.

problems.title: A parameter makes a root exceed1
problems.question: For which a does3(x+a)=4−x have its root greater than 1?
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The unique root is x=(4−3a)/4.

problems.title: Minimize a reciprocal expression on a rectangle
problems.question: Find the minimum of(3x−6y+12)/(x−2y) for 5≤x≤8,1≤y≤2.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: The expression is 3+12/(x−2y). Its denominator ranges from 1 to 6 and is positive.
steps: The minimum occurs at the largest denominator6, attained at x=8, y=1. Its value is 3+12/6=5.

problems.title: Exactly seven integer radical roots
problems.question: For which a does√((x+1)²)≤a have exactly 7 integer solutions?
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: This is|x+1|≤a. Since its centre−1 is integral, the count is 2floor(a)+1 for a≥0.

problems.title: A diagonal meets a line between side points
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD, AM:MB=1:3 and AN:ND=2:5. MN meets AC at K. Find AK:KC.
problems.idea: Keep the real domain and use exact algebra, similarity, or midpoint ratios.
formulas: Use A=0, B=u, D=v. Then M=u/4, N=2v/7, and K=t(u+v). The line MN satisfies4t+(7/2)t=1.
